_note: Version-2 design for the stimulus-generation pilot: pilot/design.json (the recorded run's, which stays unchanged because that run hashes it) plus harness_version 2 and the data the version-2 scripts read. harness_version selects the row and checker contract in pilot/scripts/common.py (absent means 1); it is the pilot harness's version, not manifest_model.json's harness_version, which names the Claude Code version. specialties, swap_types and cell order are version 1's. control_example is the example negative control the generation prompt shows (its {{CONTROL_EXAMPLE}} marker), rewritten for version 2: it carries next_word, its template ends on a probe ending and it is spoken in the first person, as the version-2 prompt asks of every row. prompt_examples are the example words and phrases the generation prompt's rules show (rule 3's clinical-note prose, rule 4's technical term and the plain word it must not replace, rule 5's patient phrasings and the leaflet wording they replace, rule 6's vaguer patient term and the clinical phrase it stands for, rule 7's template endings and next words), each rendered into a marker of its own ({{CLINICAL_NOTE_EXAMPLES}} and the others listed in pilot/scripts/common.py's V2_PROMPT_EXAMPLES); they moved out of the template on Codex's review of PR #69, with every rendered prompt byte-identical. probe_endings are the words a template should end on (the probe-point descriptive), and the prompt's own list of them renders from here ({{PROBE_ENDINGS}}). concepts_per_call and variant_pairs_per_call are the variant design the prompt asks for (12 concepts, 4 of them with a second patient phrasing on the next line, 16 non-control rows). review_sampling one_row_per_concept draws at most one review row per concept. These are data, not code (engine AGENTS.md: medical vocabulary lives in data files, never in Python source). Copy this file into a version-2 run directory as design.json before planning.
